passage: Home log, Sunday. I let the star block fall through its slot, and Manjula said "Drop!" and grabbed the block to do the same. Manjula held it flat over the hole and let go, and it bounced off the lid and rolled away. "Oops. Again," Manjula muttered, fetched it, and started from the top, this time tilting it a little. I said nothing. Yamini, Manjula's mother

qa.q: What did Manjula say when grabbing the star block?
qa.a: Manjula said "Drop!" and grabbed the block.

qa.q: What was Manjula feeling after the block bounced off the lid?
qa.a: Manjula was a bit disappointed but not discouraged; the mumbled "Oops. Again" and starting from the top show a wish to keep going.

qa.q: What could Manjula try instead of copying the drop, and why?
qa.a: Manjula could turn the block until it matches the star-shaped slot before dropping it, because copying the motion without matching the shape leaves the block on top.

qa.q: How does Yamini see the copying?
qa.a: Yamini watches quietly and lets Manjula fix the mistake alone; Yamini seems to trust that Manjula can learn from the bounce.

grounding: A toddler copies the mother's drop of the star but holds the piece flat, sees it bounce off, and starts again from the top.

passage: On the verandah of their house in a Bihar village, Aparna slid the wooden star through its slot, plop, and smiled at her son. "See, Ujjwal?" Ujjwal grabbed a star, held it flat like a biscuit and dropped it on the lid. It bounced off and rolled to the step. He fetched it, climbed back, held it flat again above the box, and let go. Bounce. He frowned and started over.

qa.q: Where did the star roll after it bounced off?
What was Ujjwal thinking as he dropped the star again?
qa.a: He seemed hopeful that dropping it just like Amma would work, and puzzled and a bit frustrated when it kept bouncing.

qa.q: What else could Aparna show Ujjwal?
qa.a: She could slowly show him how she turns the star upright before dropping it, since he copied the drop but not the angle.

qa.q: How does Ujjwal's copying look to Aparna?
qa.a: She probably finds it sweet and sees that he watched her closely but missed how she held the piece.

grounding: A toddler copies his mother dropping a star into its slot but holds it flat, so it bounces off and he starts again.

passage: Rosa knelt on the kitchen floor of their Lisbon flat and posted the green star into the sorter. "In it goes!" Emeka watched, then snatched another star, held it flat between finger and thumb, and let it fall. It clacked on the lid and skittered away. He crawled after it, came back, lifted it high above the box and dropped it flat again. Clack. He looked at Rosa, then at the star.

qa.q: What colour was the star Rosa posted?
What does Emeka's look at Rosa and then the star suggest?
qa.a: He seems puzzled and a little frustrated, trying to work out why her drop worked and his did not.

qa.q: What would you change first to help Emeka?
qa.a: Turn the star so its points match the hole before he drops it, or guide his hand once, because the angle is what he missed.

qa.q: How might Rosa feel as she watches?
qa.a: Rosa is probably amused and touched that he copies her, and patient as he tries again.

grounding: A toddler copies his mother dropping a star into a sorter but holds it flat, sees it bounce and starts from the top again.
